_comment: CI Monitor configuration. Each value is a regex; absent keys fall back to in-code defaults (see README.md). artifact_name_regex selects which run artifacts carry test-result markers worth downloading. interesting_step_regex selects which step names surface on a non-failing conclusion (genuine failures always surface regardless). deferred_verdict_step_regex selects steps whose success conclusion is not a test verdict (they always exit 0 by design, issue #309); their success line is annotated (verdict deferred to Gate). test_marker_regex locates the per-test ndjson marker. label_gate_check_regex matches a check-run name that is a process-label gate (not a substantive code/test failure); matched runs are annotated [label gate] in the summary and terminal.
_comment_test_marker: This repo matches BOTH ##GB4PC_TEST## and ##TEST## for back-compatibility while the emit side still writes ##GB4PC_TEST##. The JSON payload begins at the end of whichever alternative matched, so both markers parse correctly. Alternation order does not matter for this pair (neither marker is a prefix of the other); the full marker is simply listed first as a readable convention.
_comment_deferred_verdict: The nine deferred-verdict steps in build.yml: the eight 'Run <Class>E2ETest' steps and 'Run instrumented tests'. Each wraps its test invocation in an if/else that records outcome=success|failure to $GITHUB_OUTPUT but always exits 0 (issue #309), so the step's own Actions conclusion is always success and the real verdict is the later 'Gate on test failures' step. Deliberately narrower than interesting_step_regex, which also matches 'Build and run unit tests'--that step runs testDebugUnitTest under `set -o pipefail`, so its conclusion is an honest verdict and must NOT be annotated.
